{"status":"ready","summary":"I added a fast path for EXPRESSION_FILTER in ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp; the change is in this one file). When the expression is an AND/OR tree whose leaves are BETWEENs or comparisons (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of the filtered column (BOUND_REF 0, exact type) against non-NULL constants of the same type, the selected values are first gathered into a dense array. Each node is then evaluated as a branch-free uint8 mask and ANDed/ORed together. The mask is ANDed with validity and turned into a fresh selection vector. Anything else falls back to the existing ExpressionExecutor path unchanged.

Measured: the lineitem scan in the q19.m0 profile went from 5.12s to 4.76s CPU, and total time from 0.725s to 0.670s. `bench q19` gave -9.0%, -7.5% and -11.1% in three runs; the full bench had q19 at only -2.9% because that run was noisy. The full bench geomean was -0.1%. That run showed q08 +12.5% and q17 +9.9%, but a re-run gave +0.6% and -0.2%, and q22 went from +6.3% to -1.1%. I didn't trace the plans of those templates to rule out the new path, but the re-runs say it was noise.

Correctness check: on a temp table with NULLs (DECIMAL, INTEGER, DATE, UTINYINT columns), 4 count queries matched the same predicates rewritten with casts so they fall back to the generic path. A sum with flipped constant-on-left comparisons and != matched its hand-computed value. I did not confirm that these test filters were actually pushed down as expression filters, so they may not have exercised the new path.","generality":"This helps any table scan with a single-column filter made of AND/OR combinations of range or equality comparisons against constants, for example bucketed ranges like `(x BETWEEN a AND b) OR (x BETWEEN c AND d)`, or `(x < a OR x > b)` where the planner made it an expression filter. It covers integer-ordered types: all signed and unsigned ints up to 64 bits, DECIMAL stored as int16/32/64, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP variants.

It does not apply to floats/doubles (deliberately excluded because of NaN ordering), strings, HUGEINT/DECIMAL(38), TIME_TZ, INTERVAL, expressions with casts, functions or NOT, multi-column expressions, or calls with more than STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE selected rows (the multi-chunk path). Those all use the existing executor.

NULL handling: with no NOT and no NULL constants, a NULL input makes every leaf NULL, so the whole tree is NULL and the row is rejected. The fast path does exactly that by ANDing the mask with validity. Work is proportional to the incoming selection because only selected values are gathered.","notes":"- In the prior run, evaluating the full 2048-row vector even when the incoming selection was sparse made q19 5% slower. Gathering the selected values first is essential.
- Full-bench noise on unrelated templates is about ±10% (q08, q17); re-run individual templates before drawing conclusions.
- The plan is re-analysed on every vector call (a tree walk plus reading a few Value constants). It's cheap for small trees. Precompiling it into ExpressionFilterState would need a header change.
- Possible follow-ups:
  - Add float/double support using DuckDB's NaN-aware comparison operators.
  - Extend to VARCHAR equality ORs.
  - The lineitem scan is still about 4.76s CPU, mostly from other filters (shipinstruct string equality, BF) and decoding."}

structured_output.summary:
I added a fast path for EXPRESSION_FILTER in ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp; the change is in this one file). When the expression is an AND/OR tree whose leaves are BETWEENs or comparisons (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of the filtered column (BOUND_REF 0, exact type) against non-NULL constants of the same type, the selected values are first gathered into a dense array. Each node is then evaluated as a branch-free uint8 mask and ANDed/ORed together. The mask is ANDed with validity and turned into a fresh selection vector. Anything else falls back to the existing ExpressionExecutor path unchanged.

Measured: the lineitem scan in the q19.m0 profile went from 5.12s to 4.76s CPU, and total time from 0.725s to 0.670s. `bench q19` gave -9.0%, -7.5% and -11.1% in three runs; the full bench had q19 at only -2.9% because that run was noisy. The full bench geomean was -0.1%. That run showed q08 +12.5% and q17 +9.9%, but a re-run gave +0.6% and -0.2%, and q22 went from +6.3% to -1.1%. I didn't trace the plans of those templates to rule out the new path, but the re-runs say it was noise.

Correctness check: on a temp table with NULLs (DECIMAL, INTEGER, DATE, UTINYINT columns), 4 count queries matched the same predicates rewritten with casts so they fall back to the generic path. A sum with flipped constant-on-left comparisons and != matched its hand-computed value. I did not confirm that these test filters were actually pushed down as expression filters, so they may not have exercised the new path.
structured_output.generality:
This helps any table scan with a single-column filter made of AND/OR combinations of range or equality comparisons against constants, for example bucketed ranges like `(x BETWEEN a AND b) OR (x BETWEEN c AND d)`, or `(x < a OR x > b)` where the planner made it an expression filter. It covers integer-ordered types: all signed and unsigned ints up to 64 bits, DECIMAL stored as int16/32/64, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP variants.

It does not apply to floats/doubles (deliberately excluded because of NaN ordering), strings, HUGEINT/DECIMAL(38), TIME_TZ, INTERVAL, expressions with casts, functions or NOT, multi-column expressions, or calls with more than STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE selected rows (the multi-chunk path). Those all use the existing executor.

NULL handling: with no NOT and no NULL constants, a NULL input makes every leaf NULL, so the whole tree is NULL and the row is rejected. The fast path does exactly that by ANDing the mask with validity. Work is proportional to the incoming selection because only selected values are gathered.
structured_output.notes:
- In the prior run, evaluating the full 2048-row vector even when the incoming selection was sparse made q19 5% slower. Gathering the selected values first is essential.
- Full-bench noise on unrelated templates is about ±10% (q08, q17); re-run individual templates before drawing conclusions.
- The plan is re-analysed on every vector call (a tree walk plus reading a few Value constants). It's cheap for small trees. Precompiling it into ExpressionFilterState would need a header change.
- Possible follow-ups:
  - Add float/double support using DuckDB's NaN-aware comparison operators.
  - Extend to VARCHAR equality ORs.
  - The lineitem scan is still about 4.76s CPU, mostly from other filters (shipinstruct string equality, BF) and decoding.
